newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia alarmed by Taleban advances in Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Russia alarmed by Taleban advances in Afghanistan.

text.p: Russia expressed alarm on Saturday over events in Afghanistan and said advances there by the Taleban Islamic militia endangered stability in Central Asia.
"The situation in regions of Afghanistan adjacent to the CIS (Commonwealth of Independent States) has severely worsened," the government said in a statement carried by Itar-Tass news agency.
"A threat is building up to the security of CIS countries, especially Uzbekistan and Tajikstan," it said.
The statement said that any violation of international borders would trigger a speedy response from the CIS, successor organisation to the Soviet Union.
Earlier on Saturday the Taleban, which espouses a purist brand of Islam, entered the main northern Afghan city of Mazar-i-Sharif, a former stronghold of opposition leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum.
Dostum's military headquarters town of Shibarghan also fell to the Taleban on Saturday.
Tass said Dostum's forces were retreating towards the Afghan border with Uzbekistan. It added that Russia had evacuated its consulate staff from Mazar-i-Sharif.
Last October Russia and the former Soviet republics of Central Asia vowed to take joint action against any Afghan threat to regional security.
Around 20,000 Russian troops are deployed in war-racked Tajikistan, where they view themselves as a shield against militant Islamist extremism spreading north from Afghanistan.
Earlier this week senior Tajik security officials discussed urgent measures to reinforce the Afghan border and prevent a massive influx of refugees.
The Taleban, who seized Kabul last September, now control most of Afghanistan.
